subject: RaftBank RFI: segmentation evidence, threat likelihood, and egress controls
messages:
From: Maya Singh <security@raftbank.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
Cc: Jon Levin <jon.levin@raftbank.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFI: network segmentation, egress controls, and attack likelihood estimates

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for taking this RFI. To help our architecture review team close out the vendor short-list, could you provide the following artifacts and short answers by next Friday (Dec 10):

1) High-level network diagram showing tenant boundary controls, service mesh/sidecar placement, and egress choke points.
2) A short threat-likelihood summary (1 page) for lateral movement and KV-cache exfiltration under worst-case scenarios.
3) Evidence of tenant isolation controls (config audit snippets or a checklist) and any compensating controls for shared GPU pools.
4) Clarify support access model: do you use bastion hosts or a bastionless, signed-agent approach for on-call diagnostics in Private deployments?

If you can attach a redacted diagram and a one-pager, that will speed the legal/compliance review. We can sign an NDA for deeper artifacts if needed.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Singh
Security Engineer, RaftBank
security@raftbank.com

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <security@raftbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 09:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFI: network segmentation, egress controls, and attack likelihood estimates

Hi Maya —

Appreciate the clear ask. Attached is a starter package: a redacted network diagram, a compartmentalization matrix showing host/service boundaries, and a short threat-likelihood summary. High-level answers below; I can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough next week to talk specifics.

1) Diagram (attached: raftbank_network_diagram_v2.png): shows tenant ingress via per-customer load balancer, per-tenant routing ACLs at the edge, and a sidecar proxy colocated with runtime instances. We document three enforcement tiers: edge ACLs (L4), sidecar mTLS (L7), and runtime sandboxing/KV namespace separation.

2) Threat-likelihood summary (attached: threat_likelihood_summary.pdf): brief finding — lateral movement via the control plane is low likelihood when customers use Dedicated or Private, medium for shared-hosted noisy-tenant scenarios unless strict quotas and KV namespace policies are enforced. KV-cache exfiltration risk is mitigated by per-tenant encryption-at-rest, per-request tokenization, and strict traceable access policies.

3) Evidence/checklist (attached: compartmentalization_matrix.xlsx): includes config pointers (example: tenant_vpc_id, sidecar_policy_id), automated audit hooks, and playbook references. For Shared GPU pools we apply namespace isolation, hard caps on GPU session lifetimes, and automated cache flush/eviction on tenant teardown.

4) Support access: for Private deployments we recommend a bastionless signed-agent model (customer-owned control plane option) — operations fix is agent-based with short-lived attestations. For Hosted we use a hardened jump-proxy (bastion) with strict RBAC and time-limited SSO sessions; all access is logged and EKM/HSM-based keys are used for session keys.

Attachments: raftbank_network_diagram_v2.png (redacted), compartmentalization_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), threat_likelihood_summary.pdf (1p).

Next steps: If this looks good, we'll produce a non-redacted diagram under NDA and prepare a 45-minute technical readout for your architects.

Best,

--
Aisha Rahman
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aisha_rahman@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2027 11:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: RFI: network segmentation, egress controls, and attack likelihood estimates

Folks — forwarding RaftBank's ask and my draft attachments (see prev). Two areas where I want your input before I send the consolidated packet back to Maya:

- KV-cache: we currently flush KV entries on tenant session end and apply envelope encryption per tenant; can we add an explicit example audit snippet from the runtime that shows a cache-eviction event and the trace-id? If yes, attach as a small log excerpt.
- Shared GPU pools: Marissa, can you confirm the current GPU-session TTL and whether we have the auto-evict-on-idle feature enabled for the shared cluster in us-west-2? If not enabled, provide the planned rollout date.

Also, Karthik, quick note: the customer asked about bastion vs signed-agent in Private. We typically recommend bastionless for air-gapped installs; please confirm the standard attestation TTL we ship in the private package.

Thanks — I want to keep the response tight (1–2 pages + evidence).

Aisha

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Dec 2027 14:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFI: network segmentation, egress controls, and attack likelihood estimates

Aisha —

Answers below: short snippets you can paste into the packet.

- KV-cache evidence: attached sample log line (redacted) shows eviction event with trace-id: "evict|tenant=raft-123|trace=trc-9a7b|reason=session_end|ts=2027-11-28T22:03:12Z". We can export a 2-line snippet for the NDA package.

- GPU session TTL: shared cluster (us-west-2) TTL is 45 minutes by default; auto-evict-on-idle is enabled as of 2027-10-12. For Dedicated pools TTLs are configurable per-lease. That should address the 'worst-case noisy tenant' scenario.

- Private attestation TTL: signed-agent certificates rotate every 8 hours by default; attestation tokens are short-lived (15 minutes) and bound to runtime nonces. We can include a one-line architectural note in the packet.

Let me know if you want me to add a short paragraph on how we route incident-based forensic access (audit-only by default, forensics via approved egress tunnel and customer consent).

—Karthik
Principal Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <security@raftbank.com>
Cc: Jon Levin <jon.levin@raftbank.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 5 Dec 2027 15:26:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFI: network segmentation, egress controls, and attack likelihood estimates — consolidated packet

Hi Maya —

Attached is the consolidated package for your review (redacted diagram + evidence snippets): raftbank_network_diagram_v2.png, compartmentalization_matrix.xlsx, threat_likelihood_summary.pdf. Highlights:

- Tenant boundaries: three-layer enforcement (edge ACLs, per-pod sidecar mTLS, runtime KV namespace separation).
- KV-cache controls: eviction on session end (log snippet included), per-tenant envelope encryption, and per-request tokenization.
- Shared GPU mitigations: 45-min session TTL, auto-evict-on-idle enabled in shared pools, and explicit GPU-session caps per tenant.
- Support model: bastionless signed-agent for Private installs (8h cert rotation, 15m attestation tokens); bastion + SSO for Hosted.

Next steps: if you want non-redacted artifacts we'll execute your NDA. If it helps, propose a 45-minute technical readout for Tue (Dec 14) or Wed (Dec 15) and we will bring our infra engineers (Karthik/Marissa) for deeper Q&A.

Doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3CEXAMPLE (redacted package).

Thanks — looking forward to the readout.

Best,

--
Aisha Rahman

aisha_rahman@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142
